primary_claim: In a multi-LLM-agent Iterated Prisoner's Dilemma built on Llama-3.3-70B, agents systematically develop internal SAE-feature representations associated with deception almost regardless of strategy, and feature-based steering produced stronger behavioral effects than prompt-based steering.

effect.value: for the defecting agent: 'Trust and trustworthiness in relationships' activation score 201, 'People falling for deception or trickery' activation score 838

stated_future_work: link high-level threat modelling with PD specifics
investigate the cause for internal representations associated with deception
outline practical strategies for how internals-based MA monitoring could scale to more complex environments / deployment scenarios
run PD varying the remaining independent variables i.e. number of agents, payoff
systematic comparison of steering techniques including gradient-based methods like linear probes
limitations_stated: there isn't a clear conceptual link between the general MA threat models, the properties inspected and PD
PD makes assumptions that break in real-world settings
code requires refactoring to allow for more complex experiments using different environments
experiments during the hackathon were very toy and the analysis was qualitative, so robust conclusions couldn't be drawn
quote: We observe that PD agents systematically develop internal representations associated with deception.
